key_insight: Policy mirror descent can converge linearly even when the critic is updated with only one TD step per iteration, and this still extends to a stochastic single-trajectory setting with explicit sample-complexity guarantees.
engineering_relevance: This reduces the need for expensive policy-evaluation loops or reset-heavy rollouts, making regularized RL more practical for long-horizon control under limited data access.
method: Exact coordinate-wise Bellman updates with a persistent critic and constant actor stepsize.
A resolvent-based auxiliary distribution plus a decaying Bellman-violation correction in the convergence proof.
Stochastic TD-PMD with a strongly convex mirror map and finite-batch TD updates on one off-policy Markov trajectory.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports global linear convergence for the exact-update case and an expected value-gap rate of \u03b5 in \~O(1/((1-\u03b3)^5 \u03c3~_b \u03b5)) transitions, with numerical results matching the theory.
watch_item: Performance depends on sufficient behavior-policy coverage; the inverse dependence on \u03c3~_b suggests weak exploration can significantly slow learning.
paper_title: Fast Regularized Policy Mirror Descent with One-Step TD Updates
